title: Set up a GenAI prompt
summary: put a one-click AI command on an LN screen, check its answer, improve it, and take it away.

tokens.v: A prompt is tied to one exact session code, and its dataset to that session's table. So the build starts on the screen the command will sit on, not in the setup sessions, and with what the answer has to say. The example's screen is Sales Order Lines. LN has no language model of its own: it keeps a list retrieved from the Infor GenAI application, and a prompt that names no model uses the one that service marks as default.

phases.title: Model the dataset
phases.route: Tools ➔ Application Extensibility ➔ Embedded GenAI ➔ Datasets

tokens.v: A dataset is the LN data that travels with the question, and it is the whole of what the model is told. It starts from one main table and one index of it. The record the user is on reaches the dataset through that index, which is why both have to be the screen's own. Every field ticked is sent, so the first version takes only what the first prompt text names. The example's is six fields of a sales order line.

phases.title: Run it and check the answer

tokens.v: When the command is chosen, LN runs the dataset for the record on the screen, writes the result into the prompt text and sends it to the model. The answer opens in a window of its own. The model answers only from what the dataset sent, and a wrong answer looks the same as a right one, so the first runs are checked against the screen, once for each kind of record the prompt can meet.
